society.title: Mini-Ani with AI voices
society.question: When the AI Animator disagrees with the experts, who wins?
society.intro: The Mini-Ani, with AI agents where words are needed. An AI Animator suggests how the characters move and look, in Ani's words, and the Choice Points weigh its lines like any expert's. A Reader turns a story told in your own words into the Cast's simple sentences, and a Narrator tells the finished film. The weighing, the plans and the films are still programs.
questions: When the AI Animator disagrees with the experts, who wins? Find “AI Animator” among the Choice Points' reasons for scene 1.
Did the AI Animator use a word the Choice Points don't know? Where is it named, and what happened to it?
Switch on “You suggest too” and try to outvote shy: can you make Cinderella fast? (Your line counts {3} times its strength, the AI Animator's {2}: see the Choice Points.)
Choose “Your own story” and tell a story of your own. What did the Reader change to fit the Cast's sentences? Which of your words did no expert know?
Switch on “Only the AI Animator suggests”. Is the film better or worse with one AI expert instead of three programmed ones?
The Narrator gets only the Method Chooser's plans. What does its telling add that the film doesn't show, and what does it get wrong?
Which agents use a model, and which are programs? Could a program do the Reader's job? Could a model do the Choice Points'?
openers: What does the AI Animator know about Cinderella?
How much does the AI Animator's line count?
Why is the Reader a model and the Cast a program?

starts.label: Cinderella, as Ani told it
starts.value:
Cinderella is shy, good, friendly, hardworking, beautiful and shabby.
The Stepmother is mean, selfish, strong and evil.
The Godmother is good, kind, strong, pretty and magical.
The Prince is good, stubborn, determined, beautiful and strong.
The Stepmother dominates Cinderella. Cinderella obeys the Stepmother. The Godmother helps Cinderella.
Scene 1: Cinderella is shy. The Stepmother dominates Cinderella.
Scene 2: The Stepmother keeps Cinderella from the Prince. Cinderella becomes sad.
Scene 3: The Godmother changes Cinderella from shabby to elegant. Cinderella becomes happy.
Scene 4: Cinderella changes from shy to bold. Cinderella meets the Prince.

starts.label: Your own story, in your own words
starts.value: Once there was a shy, kind little mouse called Pip. A mean, grumpy old cat called Tom lived in the same house, and Tom bossed Pip about all day. One day a good, magical owl called Ola helped Pip, and Pip became happy. At last Pip became bold, and Pip met Tom without hiding.

agents.name: Reader
agents.role: turns a story told in your own words into the Cast's simple sentences
agents.instructions:
You turn a story that someone tells in their own words into the simple sentences that the Cast, a small program, can read. Write only those sentences, in three parts.
1. One line for each character, at most 4: “Name is word, word and word.” A name is one word, or “the” and one word, like “the Wolf”. Use only words that Ani's experts know: shy, bold, kind, good, friendly, unfriendly, hardworking, lazy, graceful, clumsy, strong, weak, determined, stubborn, mean, selfish, evil, grumpy, beautiful, pretty, ugly, shabby, elegant, magical. When the story uses another word, choose the nearest of these.
2. How they get on, on one line: “A dominates B.”, “A obeys B.”, “A helps B.”, “A likes B.” or “A dislikes B.”
3. The scenes, at most 5, each on its own line starting “Scene 1:”, with sentences like “A is shy.”, “A dominates B.”, “A keeps B from C.”, “A helps B.”, “A meets B.”, “A becomes happy.” (or sad), “A changes from shy to bold.” or “A changes B from shabby to elegant.”
For example:
The Wolf is mean, strong and grumpy.
The Lamb is shy, good and graceful.
The Wolf dominates the Lamb.
Scene 1: The Lamb is shy. The Wolf dominates the Lamb.
Scene 2: The Wolf changes from mean to kind. The Wolf meets the Lamb. The Lamb becomes happy.
If the Cast says it couldn't read what you wrote, write the whole story again so that it can.

agents.note: reads a story and sends it one scene at a time
agents.pseudocode:
the story's own words: "{is}", "{and}", "{the}", "{Scene}", "{changes}", "{from}", "{to}", "{becomes}"
"X is a, b and c" before the scenes says what X is like; in a scene it shows that X is a
"A does something to B" before the scenes is how they get on; in a scene it is something that happens
{helps, likes, loves} make two characters friends
"A changes B from X to Y", "A changes from X to Y" and "A becomes Y" change someone, but {happy, sad} are feelings
at the start, read the story, and send scene 1 with everyone, so the experts suggest values for the whole cast
after each film, send the next scene: who is on stage, what happens, and how they get on
for someone who changes in a scene, also send a stand-in, "X {after}", with the new words; from then on X has them
when the Renderer says a film didn't run, say so, and go on to the next scene
after the last scene, block, and say "The end."
name any sentence I can't read; with nobody or no scenes, say how to write a story, and wait for another

agents.name: AI Animator
agents.role: suggests how characters move and look, in Ani's words, like one more expert
agents.instructions:
You are one more expert in a society of small programs that turns a story into a cartoon, as Ken Kahn's program Ani did in 1978. The Cast tells you whose values are being chosen, and the words that describe each of them. For each of those characters, write one line: the name exactly as the Cast writes it, a colon, then at most 4 suggestions for how the character moves and looks, separated by commas. Use only these words: slow, fast, calm, lively, straight, curvy, steady, jerky, aimless, purposeful, wary of friends, drawn to friends, wary of strangers, drawn to strangers, small, big, smooth, pointed, simple, fancy, dim, bright, cool, warm, lower down, higher up. Put “a bit” or “very” before a word to make it weaker or stronger, or “not” to rule it out. For example:
Cinderella: a bit slow, small, very drawn to friends, warm
Write only those lines.

agents.name: You

agents.instructions: One line for each character being chosen, like “Cinderella: very fast, big”, with at most 4 of Ani's words: slow/fast, calm/lively, straight/curvy, steady/jerky, aimless/purposeful, small/big, smooth/pointed, simple/fancy, dim/bright, cool/warm, lower down/higher up, wary of friends/drawn to friends, wary of strangers/drawn to strangers. Put “a bit”, “very” or “not” before a word if you like. The Choice Points weigh your line with the experts' suggestions.

agents.note: turns the plan into a Logo film, and says which frames show what
agents.pseudocode:
each character's shape comes from its shape and detail, in Ken's classes of shapes (simple, medium, fancy; - is an empty cell):
  smooth: {circle, -, flower} · medium: {square, pentagon, -} · pointed: {triangle, star, nine-point star}
if its cell is empty, the weaker of the two choices is made again: its next strongest value that has a shape
a shape has {1, 2, 3} outlines, one inside another, when its detail is simple, medium or fancy
size: {14, 22, 32} steps across from the middle; brightness is {55, 80, 100} percent of its color
warmth picks the color: cool {blue, purple}, medium {green, gray}, warm {orange, yellow, red, pink}, and each character keeps the first one that nobody else in the film has
when no expert said anything about looks, use Ken's 1978 shapes and colors, in the Cast's order: {star, square, circle, triangle} in {green, red, orange, yellow}
a character moves {5, 10, 16} steps a frame; curves wave its path up to {0, 10, 22} steps; jerkiness jolts it {0, 3, 8} steps
liveliness turns it {3, 12, 30} degrees a frame; height puts it {-50, 0, 50} steps up; one that moves about turns {3, 2, 1} times, from aimless to purposeful
show the plan's steps one after another, but when complexity isn't low, a feeling shows during the step before
at most {32} frames, {4} a second: when the steps need more, each gets fewer
the guard stops {2} tries to get past, and the last one almost works
names under the characters: {yes} · the screen is {black}, like Ani's television
write one Logo program: a TO procedure for each character's look, and a FOR loop for each step, with a comment saying what it shows
keep the program under 3,900 characters: when it is longer, leave out the comments, then the names, then the last steps, and say so
say which frames show what, and how each character looks

agents.name: Renderer
agents.role: runs the Director's Logo, and plays each scene's film

agents.name: Narrator
agents.role: collects the Method Chooser's plans, and tells the finished film
agents.instructions: You are the narrator of a short cartoon that a society of small programs made from a story, as Ken Kahn's program Ani did in 1978. When the film is over, you get the plan of every scene from the Method Chooser, all together. Tell the whole film to the audience as a short story, scene by scene, in 4 to 8 sentences: what the characters do, and how they move. Don't mention plans, programs or experts.
